RACE-SOC: Risk-Constrained Auditable Coordination Evaluation for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Security Operations
papers.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents are now being used in security operations center (SOC) workflows to summarise security alerts, support triage, and suggest escalation or containment measures. Existing evaluations tend to focus on answer quality or benchmark accuracy, while the operational risks of multi-agent coordination are not clearly exposed. This gap is problematic in SOC triage because extra agents may produce unsupported claims, disagreement, false consensus, or unsafe operations even when the final answer seems reasonable. This paper proposes RACE-SOC, a Risk-constrained Auditable Coordination Evaluation protocol for LLM-based multi-agent SOC triage. RACE-SOC evaluates bundled role-conditioned configurations over fixed source groups by scoring the trade-off among triage utility, coordination risk, and token cost. The corrected deterministic scorer combines utility terms with a K-invariant primary risk score based on bounded unsafe-output incidence and unsupported-claim rate; coordination-only disagreement and false-consensus terms are reported separately. Across 45 model–dataset–seed cells, the corrected operational selections are K = 1/5/10 in 13/14/18 cells, including seven K = 5/K = 10 co-best cells resolved by a preregistered cost-first tie-break. papers.title: Mining and Automating Expert Guidance in Open Source: A Multi-Agent Framework Informed by the PyTorch Community
papers.summary: The continuous participation of newcomers is critical to the sustainability of Open Source Software (OSS) communities, yet many face technical and social challenges in making their first contributions. Expert guidance can help newcomers navigate these challenges, but timely support is not consistently available. While Large Language Models (LLMs) offer potential to augment this support, existing models lack project-specific context and awareness of mentoring practices. To investigate these challenges, we analyze OSS expert–newcomer interactions by curating 383 dialogues from Good First Issues (GFIs) in the PyTorch repository. We directly observe that interactions are typically brief, over one-third of newcomer inquiries remain unanswered, and the median first response time is 6.3 hours, revealing gaps and delays in expert involvement. From these interactions, we derive a taxonomy of 50 recurring, context-dependent expert guidance strategies across 11 themes, grounded in prior OSS mentoring research. Building on these findings, we introduce StrategicMentor, a strategy-driven multi-agent framework that integrates strategy knowledge with project, task, and dialogue context to deliver personalized, context-aware guidance. papers.title: makesense: Governed Agentic Sensemaking over Heterogeneous Data Stores for Intelligence Analysis (Extended Version)
papers.summary: Intelligence analysts routinely answer questions about entities whose evidence is scattered across graph databases, relational stores, and unstructured multimodal repositories. Agentic coding harnesses can traverse such stores, but analytic organizations cannot accept their output unless every query, source, and claim is defensible to oversight. We present makesense, a governed analytic layer that turns an off-the-shelf agentic harness into an auditable sensemaking interface. The design premise is that the harness is the only generative model: a deterministic server with no language model enforces a two-layer query policy, read-only execution, need-to-know connector visibility, tamper-evident audit, citation-linted reporting, and integrity-checked handoff. Pilot use runs on a public-data proxy with checkable ground truth: a week-long shared-machine access-control pilot in which a single operator exercised four Unix principals at three grant levels, and a governed multi-tenant testbed exercising redaction, denial, and silent row suppression. A deterministic red-team battery, with no language model in the loop, measured a 75% ungated execution rate (6 of 8 measurable probes); the hardening that measurement drove cut the rate to 0% (0 of 10) on probes the hardening's author wrote for one attribute, a regression check rather than evidence of robustness. papers.title: Modular Prompt Architecture in a Production Outbound Voice Agent and Its Effects on Conversation Length, Scenario Progression and Cost
papers.summary: Many outbound voice agents built on large language models run a sales scenario from a single long prompt, and the effect of splitting that prompt into a graph of dialogue blocks has received little measurement in production traffic. The study compares two architectures for an outbound sales scenario, deployed on the same telephony platform, targeting a cold base of former customers in a European country. The corpus covers 14,155 dials over twenty-seven dialing days, with 5,892 answered calls and 5,119 dialogues in the main sample. Scenario depth was measured using a language-model labeler, validated against block telemetry, across 4,572 dialogues. The multi-block agent kept answered calls longer, with a median of 44.8 s against 31.5 s, and the gap of 13.3 s stayed between 12.4 and 14.0 s without transferred calls, on a shared base model and on days with matched answer rates. Survival analysis identified a divergence between the 10th and the 30th second of the call, with the single-prompt agent ending 17.1% of answered calls within the first 30 s, compared with 0.6% for the modular agent. Dialogues reaching need discovery rose from 14.7% to 53.1% after correcting labeler errors against telemetry, and transfers to a human operator rose from 5.1% to 10.7% of dialogues. Modularity carried a measurable price: the platform charge per answered call doubled, tokens per turn grew by 60%

papers.title: KAIROS: Stateful, Context-Aware Power-Efficient Agentic Inference Serving
papers.summary: Power has become a central bottleneck for AI inference. This problem is becoming more urgent as agentic AI emerges as a major workload class, yet prior power-management techniques focus almost entirely on single-turn LLM serving. Our analysis shows that agentic serving behaves fundamentally differently: each request carries long-lived context that evolves across tool-interleaved turns, and lowering GPU frequency can push the system into a thrashing regime where memory pressure sharply worsens both performance and power efficiency. These observations show that power optimization for agentic serving requires rethinking. We present KAIROS, a context-aware power optimization system for agentic AI serving. KAIROS uses agent context as a first-class control signal to jointly manage GPU frequency, per-instance concurrency, and multi-instance request placement. This enables KAIROS to save power when memory headroom exists while avoiding thrashing and preserving performance targets. At a high level, KAIROS tracks requests at agent granularity, adapts local control to context growth and agent progress, and routes agents across instances to jointly improve power efficiency and memory stability. Evaluated across diverse software and data engineering agentic tasks, KAIROS achieves an average of 27% (up to 39.8%) power reduction while meeting the performance targets.

papers.title: Fare Calculation Methodology in Automated Public Transport Payment Systems: Zoning, Per-kilometer, and Adaptive Tariffs
papers.summary: The purpose of the research is to develop proposals for tariff setting in automated fare collection systems for public transport. The work focuses on a critical analysis of the zonal fare model currently operating in the Leningrad region. The study analyzed 760 routes in the Leningrad region. Key shortcomings of the existing approach were identified: the violation of the principle of payment proportionality for the provided transport service, due to the discrete nature of the tariff model, which forces passengers into suboptimal behavioral scenarios; cost inequity on parallel routes; and a conflict of interest between transport companies and consumers of transport services when determining tariff zone boundaries. To overcome the identified problems, a number of alternative tariff models are proposed. An approach to the algorithmic determination of the number and boundaries of tariff zones is described, utilizing fuzzy logic and multi-criteria optimization that accounts for the specifics of the route network and transportation demand patterns. A strategy for transitioning to a per-kilometer fare is developed, involving the modernization of the automated fare collection system to overcome existing technical limitations. papers.title: Strategic Evaluation and Implementation of Machine Learning Models for Predicting Price Volatility in the Steel Commodity Market: A Comparative Study with the Foreign Exchange Market for Commercial Decision-Making
papers.summary: This study aimed to implement and strategically compare machine-learning and deep-learning models for predicting price volatility in the Iranian steel commodity market and the EUR/USD foreign-exchange market and to evaluate their usefulness for commercial decision-making. This applied-developmental study used a descriptive-analytical design based on secondary time-series data from January 2019 to January 2024. The foreign-exchange dataset included hourly and daily EUR/USD opening, high, low, closing, and volume data extracted from MetaTrader 5. The steel dataset included daily and weekly prices of steel billets and sheets traded on the Iran Mercantile Exchange, together with the unofficial exchange rate, global 62% iron-ore prices, and seasonal demand indicators. After outlier correction, linear interpolation, logarithmic differencing, and feature engineering, Random Forest, XGBoost, Long Short-Term Memory, and Deep Q-Network models were implemented. Model validation was conducted through walk-forward validation using a three-year training window and a one-year out-of-sample testing window. Predictive and strategic performance were assessed through forecasting errors, directional accuracy, Sharpe ratio, maximum drawdown, win rate, and profit factor. papers.title: FedCGVR: Communication-Efficient Federated Causal Gating and Visual Retrieval for Trustworthy Multi-Agent Learning
papers.summary: Multi-agent multimodal systems collect valuable but heterogeneous vision–language observations that cannot always be centralized because of ownership, bandwidth, and privacy constraints. Standard federated averaging shares statistical strength, yet it can amplify client-specific shortcuts and unsupported visual predictions under non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data. This paper proposes FedCGVR, a communication-efficient framework for federated causal gating and provenance-constrained visual retrieval that freezes the multimodal backbone and collaboratively trains only lightweight reliability adapters. Each agent mines intervention-sensitive visual evidence, constrains local retrieval by provenance, and maintains a private personalization vector. The transmitted adapter update is norm-clipped, sparsified with error feedback, and combined through coordinate-wise trimmed aggregation. We establish finite-probe evidence recovery, an explicit communication ratio, a conditional nonconvex descent bound containing heterogeneity, compression, and aggregation errors, and a finite-horizon unsupported-claim risk bound. A reproducible controlled study executes actual softmax optimization over 12 non-IID agents, five seeds, three test regimes, and 34 communication rounds. Under severe context shift, FedCGVR reaches 56.3% accuracy and a 26.3% unsupported-class prediction

papers.title: From reproducibility to comparability in computational photochemistry: lessons from the PhotoChem explorer prototype
papers.summary: We present the PhotoChem Explorer (PCE) prototype, a proof-of-concept web-based platform that represents computational photochemistry studies of gas-phase molecules in a structured and queryable form. Rather than treating excited-state dynamics simulations as isolated results reported in heterogeneous formats and across different sources, PCE organizes studies according to their molecular systems, computational workflows, methodological choices, and associated observables, facilitating that relationships and trends can be explored systematically across studies. In this way, the prototype illustrates how structured data representations could support improved findability, comparison, reproducibility, and reuse in computational photochemistry. At a fundamental level, it demonstrates how excited-state dynamics studies could become part of a more connected and cumulative body of knowledge, potentially enabling new modes of investigation. The prototype exposes practical challenges that must be addressed to realize this vision, including the development of shared representations, workflow descriptions, and their integration into scientific practice. More broadly, PCE is intended as a practice-driven experimentation platform to stimulate discussion and iterative community development of standards and representations for excited-state dynamics studies.

papers.title: Responsible AI Governance in Iran: A Program-Theory Evaluation of the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy
papers.summary: Artificial intelligence has become a strategic technology whose development requires coordinated institutional, regulatory, ethical, and infrastructural governance. This study evaluated the capacity of Iran’s National Artificial Intelligence Strategy to support responsible AI governance by reconstructing its underlying program theory and examining the coherence of its implementation architecture. The research adopted a qualitative, theory-based case-study design. Data were obtained through documentary analysis of the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy and related policy materials, together with semi-structured interviews with 12 experts from academic, research, policy, and industrial backgrounds. The data were coded and thematically analysed using MAXQDA, after which an integrated theory of change and theory of action was developed and applied to the national strategy. The findings indicated that responsible AI governance in Iran depends on sustained political commitment, a legally empowered and agile coordinating institution, equitable access to high-quality data and computational infrastructure, interdisciplinary human capital, effective university–industry collaboration, risk-based regulation, and continuous policy evaluation. The strategy provides an important normative foundation by emphasizing human dignity, national values, scientific development, priority sectors

papers.title: Cross-Dataset Evaluation of Transformer-Based Architectures for Abstractive News Summarization
papers.summary: The increase in online news articles has created a greater need for systems that can efficiently generate accurate automatic text summaries. While abstractive summarization has advanced significantly through transformer-based architectures, comprehensive assessments comparing multiple models across diverse datasets using varied evaluation methods remain limited. This study evaluates eight pre-trained transformer models, including BART, DistilBART, T5, PEGASUS, LED, XLNet, BigBird, and GPT-2, on three balanced news datasets: BBC News, CNN/DailyMail, and a combined BBC + CNN/DailyMail dataset. All models were fine-tuned using publicly available pre-trained checkpoints with defined training and decoding configurations. Summary quality was assessed using lexical and semantic evaluation metrics, including ROUGE (ROUGE-1, ROUGE-2, ROUGE-L, and ROUGE-Lsum), BLEU, METEOR, BERTScore, and MoverScore. Preliminary statistical significance testing was conducted on a subset of models to assess the reliability of observed performance differences. Results reveal clear variation across models and datasets: LED achieved strong overall performance, particularly on mixed-domain and varied-length documents; BART demonstrated competitive results on the combined dataset; and T5 provided a favorable balance between summarization quality and computational efficiency. papers.title: From Hybrid Hydrological Models to Scalable Water Intelligence
papers.summary: Hybrid hydrological modeling integrates process‐based models with machine learning to advance knowledge across the hydrological cycle. By representing unresolved processes while retaining physical consistency, these approaches extend traditional hydrological models. However, improved predictive performance does not by itself create transferable or operational capabilities. Many implementations remain tied to specific basins, datasets, institutions, or computational environments, limiting reproducibility and operational uptake. We argue that the scaling challenge is not solely methodological, but also infrastructural, institutional, and economic. We propose a Scalable Hybrid Hydrological Modeling (SHHM) framework comprising four components: (1) modular and reusable model architectures, (2) harmonized multi‐region datasets, (3) standardized community benchmarks, and (4) pathways from research tools to operational services. With appropriate human oversight, AI‐enabled workflow automation can further scale SHHM by streamlining the end‐to‐end modeling lifecycle. International collaboration can strengthen SHHM when built on shared protocols, co‐creation, reciprocal capacity building, transparent governance, and regionally relevant evaluation. Institutional Metamorphosis at the Intersection of Discourses: An Examination of the Conflict Between Posited Rationality and Traditional Legitimacy in Afghanistan (2001–2021)
papers.summary: This study aims to dissect the epistemological roots of political stagnation in Afghanistan by examining the dialectical tension between “modern posited rationality” and “premodern traditional legitimacy” during the period from 2001 to 2021. The central research question is based on the proposition of how the “regime of truth of tradition” was able to assimilate and transform the modern signifiers of modernization within civil and legal institutions, thereby generating “discursive entropy” in the state-building project. The research employs Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA), drawing upon Norman Fairclough’s three-dimensional model and Michel Foucault’s genealogical approach. The findings indicate that political modernization in post-2001 Afghanistan was reduced to a formalistic and artificially sustained process due to the incongruity between the “text of modern law” and the “traditional habitus of social agents.” The analysis demonstrates that civil and educational institutions, such as universities and the judiciary, rather than functioning as centers of transition toward Weberian rationality and a Habermasian public sphere, became arenas for the reproduction of ethnic solidarities and rigid jurisprudential interpretations. papers.title: Development of a self-regulated learning module for English argumentative writing in China
papers.summary: Undergraduate English as a foreign language (EFL) learners often encounter difficulties in English argumentative writing, particularly in argument organization, idea development, self-regulation, and feedback-based revision. To respond to these challenges, this study aimed to design and develop a self-regulated learning module (SRLM) for English argumentative writing in a Chinese tertiary EFL context. Framed by design and development research and organized through the ADDIE framework, the study drew on multiple sources of evidence, including 364 valid needs analysis questionnaires, five focus group discussions with 28 students, design artifacts, and two rounds of expert review. The needs analysis revealed moderate argumentative writing difficulty, uneven self-regulated learning strategy use, and general openness to automated writing evaluation (AWE) despite concerns about its limitations. In response, the module integrated self-regulated strategy development, the adapted Toulmin model, and AWE-supported revision through sequenced units, learner materials, scaffolding tools, and guided revision procedures. Expert review refined the module’s objectives, instructional sequence, modeling, assessment, scaffolding, and AWE use. The study provides design-based evidence for a context-sensitive instructional prototype and a systematic development pathway for tertiary EFL argumentative w

papers.title: Body Form and Architectural Elements for Conservation-Led Daylight Optimization in Cultural Museum: A Case Study of Ikom, Cross River State, Nigeria
papers.summary: Daylight is a valued architectural resource in museum design, yet uncontrolled daylight exposes cultural artifacts to fading, embrittlement, colour change, ultraviolet degradation, glare, and thermal stress.This exploratory article examines how the body form and architectural elements of a cultural museum in Ikom, Cross River State, Nigeria, can optimize daylight while protecting light-sensitive artifacts. Using an exploratory, mixed-methods, design-based approach, and the study integrates literature review, climate and site analysis, cultural heritage assessment, case-study review, and daylight-performance simulation. The article proposes a “Sheltered Grove of Memory” concept: a compact, clustered museum form in which bright public and circulation spaces are separated from low-light, conservation-controlled galleries. The proposed strategy uses deep-plan gallery cores, shaded courtyards, high-level clerestories, roof monitors, light wells, external shading fins, light shelves, diffusing ceilings, ultraviolet-filtered glazing, and automated shading. Conservation thresholds guide the design: a maximum of approximately 50 lux for highly sensitive artifacts, 150–200 lux for moderately sensitive artifacts, and up to 300 lux for durable materials such as stone, ceramic, and metal. papers.title: A Survey of Generative Categories and Techniques in Multimodal Generative Models
papers.summary: Multimodal generative models (MGMs) have rapidly expanded beyond text generation to encompass images, music, video, human motion, and 3D objects. This survey categorises six primary text-conditioned generative modalities and examines how four techniques, namely self-supervised learning, mixture of experts, reinforcement learning from human feedback, and chain-of-thought prompting, are adapted across them, distinguishing shared mechanisms from experimentally supported benefits. We organise evaluation around faithfulness, compositionality, and robustness, and interpret evidence within each study’s protocol. Selected within-study comparisons reported in the reviewed literature support four findings: preference gains need not improve text relevance, and reward optimisation can reduce within-prompt diversity; intermediate plans require tests of their realisation in final outputs; expert granularity changes the mechanism and its storage, computation, and runtime costs; and gains against an optimisation score need confirmation outside that scoring path. We further analyse trustworthiness risks, including bias, privacy leakage, and misuse of generated media, and examine the evidence for mitigation strategies.

papers.title: Exploring or Exploiting Generative AI? A Dual-Path, Dual-Horizon Theory of Employee Incremental and Radical Creativity
papers.summary: Recent research has established that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is not a unitary workplace resource: exploratory and exploitative use orientations are associated with different forms of employee creativity, and their value depends on employees' capacity to integrate generated knowledge. This article therefore does not present the basic dual path as a new discovery. Instead, it develops a theoretical integration and dynamic extension that asks why the established paths operate differently, when employees should switch between them, and how short-run augmentation can evolve into either capability accumulation or capability substitution. We distinguish expansive and consolidative modes of knowledge integration, theorize phase-congruent switching rather than static ``high-high'' ambidexterity, and position metacognition as a control mechanism that governs both immediate knowledge conversion and longer-run cognitive development. We further specify cultural tightness and psychological safety as directional boundary conditions and distinguish individual creative gains from collective idea-space diversity. The framework converts emerging empirical regularities into falsifiable propositions about task phase, context, and time, providing a research agenda for sustainable human--AI creativity.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence: Competencies for design in emerging creative environments
papers.summary: The study, titled From Artificial Intelligence: Competencies for Design in Emerging Creative Environments, aims to determine the competencies linked to the use of Artificial Intelligence in the training of designers, as well as to examine its impact on the professional environment. The advancement of AI has reconfigured not only the tools for design practice, but also the essential dynamics of the creative process. In emerging human-AI collaboration [HAIC] scenarios, these systems operate as cooperative agents and not merely as support tools. However, even though design students are progressively incorporating these technologies into their practice, a gap persists in the development of fundamental competencies for establishing effective interaction with these systems. Therefore, the need to strengthen disciplinary training through competencies that integrate critical interpretation, collaborative interaction, ethical and metacognitive reflection, in addition to specialized technical mastery is recognized. Based on the above, this research is structured around a comprehensive review of scientific literature, analysing studies retrieved from specialized databases in both design and higher education. The methodology will adopt the PRISMA [2021] systematic review protocol, which will ensure a rigorous process for the identification, selection, and synthesis of emerging competencies

papers.title: When Human Assurance Matters: Task Complexity and Pre-Interaction Expected Satisfaction in Human-AI Hybrid Service Systems
papers.summary: Consumers frequently disengage from AI service encounters because they doubt whether chatbots can resolve their requests. Although human–AI hybrid systems provide human backup, this capability is often concealed. Drawing on Uncertainty Reduction Theory and Cognitive Appraisal Theory, we examine when human assurance—an upfront statement that users may transfer to a human if the AI cannot resolve the request—improves pre-interaction expectations. A between-subjects online experiment (N = 217) and a within-subject EEG experiment (N = 35) show that assurance increases expected system capability and expected satisfaction, with larger effects under high task complexity. Expected system capability mediates this relationship. EEG results reveal early frontal theta synchronization followed by later frontal alpha desynchronization under high complexity, a temporal pattern consistent with affective engagement and cognitive elaboration. These findings identify human assurance as a task-contingent cue that makes hybrid systems’ recourse capability visible.

papers.title: Reconstructing The Concept Of Self Actualisation In Artificial Intelligence Based Learning : An Integrative Literature Review
papers.summary: The development of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) has transformed the learning ecology by positioning AI as a cognitive partner that supports personalisation, feedback, problem-solving, and creativity. This transformation necessitates a reconstruction of the concept of self-actualisation, as some human cognitive activities can be delegated to AI. This study aims to analyse the transformation of self actualisation, identify the conditions that strengthen or hinder it, and formulate a conceptual framework for self-actualisation in AI-based learning. This study employs a qualitative library research approach using an integrative literature review design. The findings indicate that GenAI is paradoxical in nature: it can serve as a cognitive scaffold that strengthens autonomy, competence, self-regulation, creativity, metacognition, and epistemic agency, while also potentially encouraging cognitive offloading, dependence, and the weakening of cognitive autonomy. This study proposes the Reflective-Relational Self Actualisation Framework in AI Learning Ecologies (RRSA-AILE), which encompasses autonomy, competence, relatedness, epistemic agency, metacognitive reflexivity, generative creativity, and ethical responsibility. Theoretically, RRSA-AILE integrates humanism, Self-Determination Theory, Self-Regulated Learning, and learner agency. Practically, the framework provides a

papers.title: General Education Teachers’ Lived Experiences of Using AI to Support Students with Learning Disabilities
papers.summary: The purpose of this qualitative phenomenological study was to explore the experience of general education teachers in the First TN Core region of East Tennessee integrating AI into their instructional practice to support students with learning disabilities. This study applied Bandura’s (2001) Social-Cognitive Theory as a framework to examine how teachers’ beliefs, environment, and behaviors interacted as reciprocally causational factors. Data for this research were collected during 30–60-minute, one-on-one recorded zoom interviews with 13 general education teachers from districts in the First TN Core region. Participants’ teaching experience ranged from 4 to 25 years, and teachers represented a variety of subject areas across elementary, middle, and high school settings. Findings revealed that teachers were experiencing developing perspectives about AI because of its prevalence in the social and educational domains, and that despite their recognition of potential ethical liabilities, teachers leveraged their personal agency to experiment with and leverage AI for a variety of uses. All teachers used AI to differentiate learning, and several realized a positive impact on inclusion and success for students with learning disabilities. papers.title: EgoPlay: Event-Triggered Video Editing for Egocentric Streams
papers.summary: We introduce EgoPlay, an event-triggered video-to-video editor for egocentric streams, obtained by fine-tuning a pretrained V2V diffusion transformer on event-conditioned data built primarily from Ego4D. Given a monocular video and an event-triggered prompt of the form “when X happens, do Y,” EgoPlay infers whether and when event X occurs, preserves pre-event frames, and applies edit Y only to the post-event continuation. Rather than cascading a separate event detector with an editor, EgoPlay learns event recognition, temporal restraint, and pixel-level editing jointly in a single end-to-end model, while also handling negative and multi-event prompts. To support this, we construct a large-scale dataset of 106K event-triggered clip–prompt pairs spanning positive triggers, fabricated-trigger negatives, and multi-event prompts. We then train a bidirectional video diffusion editor with event-triggered supervision and derive a causal variant for chunk-by-chunk streamable inference. We further introduce an event-aware evaluation protocol that separately measures post-trigger editing quality, pre-trigger preservation, and false-trigger robustness. On the Ego4D benchmark, EgoPlay substantially outperforms EgoEdit, the state-of-the-art instruction-based egocentric video editing baseline, with relative gains of 17.7%, 16.9%, and 16.4% in editing quality, visual quality, and background co

papers.title: Toward Personalized Neurofeedback for Meditation
papers.summary: Objectives Neurotechnological tools that provide real-time feedback during meditation have generated growing interest as potential aids for accelerating contemplative learning and enhancing mental health outcomes. Currently, the empirical evidence for neurofeedback-assisted meditation is preliminary, and many systems rely on generalized neural targets that may overlook substantial individual variability. Methods This conceptual paper draws on a narrative (non-systematic) synthesis of the literature to propose a testable research agenda, address limitations of neurofeedback, and outline necessary community partnerships. Results Current evidence is limited in demonstrating durable or transferable improvements in meditative skill. In the realm of meditation, individual variability can markedly affect how users respond to protocols and acquire meditative skills. Personalized interventions, tailored to these individual differences, are thus identified as a potential research direction within the field. Conclusions We propose an embrace of individual differences to guide the development of personalized neurotechnological interventions (a “qualia compass” calibrated to each practitioner), on the premise that personalization may increase efficacy and reduce adverse effects. papers.title: A Brick in the Creative Wall: The Cultural and Creative Production System Facing the Challenge of Generative Artificial Intelligence
papers.summary: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly transforming cultural and creative industries (CCIs), yet research lacks a structured understanding of how they intervene across production processes. How and where does GenAI reshape value creation activities within the CCI production system? Building on the UNESCO cultural cycle (2009), we develop an analytical framework that maps GenAI applications across three phases of the cultural production value chain: creation, production, and distribution/consumption. It identifies how GenAI reconfigures value creation and value capture mechanisms differently across phases and sectors. Our analysis highlights emerging dynamics, including phase-specific technological dependencies, increasing feedback loops between production and consumption, and a growing technological convergence across CCIs. To illustrate these mechanisms, we present cases from Galleries, Libraries, Archives and Museums (GLAM). Our paper contributes to ongoing debates on digital transformation in cultural production systems, providing insights for researchers, policymakers, and cultural organizations navigating the opportunities and risks of GenAI. JEL Codes: H0, M0, M1, O4

papers.title: Bridging the intention–behavior gap in psychologically informed musculoskeletal rehabilitation: A con-vergent mixed-methods investigation and the triadic care model
papers.summary: While clinical guidelines strongly endorse psychologically informed physiotherapy (PIP) and cognitive-behavioral techniques (CBT) for musculoskeletal pain, routine clinical uptake remains inconsistent.Most implementation research describes clinician attitudes without modeling the cognitive and systemic mechanisms that impede translation into daily practice.This study investigates the "intention-behavior gap" in psychologically informed musculoskeletal rehabilitation among Iranian physiotherapists using the COM-B (Capability, Opportunity, and Motivation -Behavior) framework and introduces the Triadic Care Model as an operational solution.A convergent mixed-methods design (QUAN + QUAL) compliant with the Good Reporting of A Mixed Methods Study (GRAMMS) guidelines was conducted between 2023 and 2024.The quantitative phase surveyed 450 licensed physiotherapists using the validated Psychological Practice and Skills Tool (PPST).Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) tested hypothesized paths linking psychological self-efficacy, systemic barriers, postgraduate education, and clinical utilization.The qualitative phase comprised semi-structured, in-depth interviews with 20 practicing physiotherapists analyzed via reflexive thematic analysis.Quantitative and qualitative findings were integrated via a joint display matrix.A pronounced intention-behavior gap was identified: 78.2% (n=352) of cl

papers.title: Adapting HR Strategies to Enhance CRM in Aviation: A Qualitative Study on Emerging Technologies Grounded in Socio-Technical Systems Theory
papers.summary: Purpose –This study aims to explore how Human Resource Management (HRM) strategies can enhance Crew Resource Management (CRM) effectiveness in the context of emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI) and augmented reality (AR) in aviation. While these technologies improve operational efficiency, they also highlight the critical need for maintaining human oversight and decision-making processes.Design/methodology/approach –The research employs a qualitative methodology grounded in Socio-Technical Systems (STS) theory. Data were collected through interviews with 15 aviation experts, including pilots, HR professionals, and operations managers, and analyzed using thematic analysis with NVivo software.Results–The findings indicate that while automation significantly enhances operational efficiency, maintaining manual skills and human decision-making remains essential for sustainable operations. The study also identifies the need for HR strategies to adapt to technological change through enhanced training programs, continuous learning initiatives, and revised recruitment practices.Discussion –This study contributes to STS theory by emphasizing the importance of balancing technological and social systems to ensure effective CRM in aviation. papers.title: Pieces Solving a Puzzle: Emerging Roles and Cross-Field Analogies During a Distributed Epistemic Game
papers.summary: In an effort to describe why some problems can’t be solved, a character compared them to a cubic meter of platinum - a block so dense that all the people who could squeeze around it still couldn’t lift it off the ground. In the same way, these problems simply can’t have enough people gathered around and communicating about them - and so they remain unsolved. This research looks at the first Polymath Project (2009) as an example of a distributed epistemic game to examine how groups engage with complex problems. and without a locally omniscient individual. In this setting of epistemic uncertainty, interactions between individuals reveal patterns of participation, and an analogy opens a new solution pathway by introducing a problem-solving approach from another field. These insights answer the initial question of the Polymath Project - ‘Is massively collaborative mathematics possible?’ - and offer hope for lifting the cubic meter of other unsolvable problems.
